subject: Intermittent TCP sessions to on-prem: MSS / offload interaction - triage
messages:
From: Alan Zhou <alan.zhou@acme-corp.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: netops@acme-corp.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:34 -0800
Subject: Intermittent failures from our app -> Redwood private nodes (port 443)

Rafael,

We've been seeing intermittent TLS session resets from our frontends to your private deployment. About ~1 in 200 connections fail with a TCP retransmit sequence and the app reports TLS handshake timeout. The pattern started after the kernel NIC firmware roll last week.

I attached a small tcpdump sample (filtered to the failing flow). Can you confirm whether anything on your side is doing MSS clamping, TCP offload, or path MTU changes?

Alan
Senior NetEng, Acme Corp
alan.zhou@acme-corp.com

Attachments: acme_tcpdump-port443-20261128.pcap (pcap, 2.3MB)
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: alan.zhou@acme-corp.com, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:35:02 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures from our app -> Redwood private nodes (port 443)

Thanks for the sample Alan — looking. Marissa/Jonas: can you pick this up as a priority? Initial hypothesis: either a MTU/MSS mismatch on the EVPN/VXLAN path or our dedicated host NIC offload interacting with the customer's ASA (we recently enabled TSO/TSO6 and GSO on the new host images).

Plan:
- Jonas: run a traceroute+TCPMSS probe from the egress host that handles Acme (I can point you to the node IDs).
- Marissa: pull kernel dmesg and host NIC offload settings; check whether we applied a per-customer iptables NAT with MSS clamp rules for this route.
- I'll coordinate with Alan for a quick capture on their edge during replication.

--
Rafael Mendes
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: alan.zhou@acme-corp.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 11:02:17 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures from our app -> Redwood private nodes (port 443)

Rafael/Marissa,

I ran an extended path probe from host redd-az2-nf-17 (handles Acme egress) toward 34.82.120.45:443. Findings:
- ICMP path MTU reports 1500 across the transit.
- Raw TCP MSS probe (SYN with MSS 1460) is accepted but subsequent SYNs in failing flows show MSS reduced to 1400 on the customer's side (SYN from them shows MSS 1400).
- Kernel offload flags on the host: TSO=on, GSO=on, GRO=on.

I uploaded path-trace-logs.txt to the shared drive link. My take: either the customer's ASA is clamping MSS down (1400) and combined with TSO/GSO it leads to large segments that get dropped on intermediate devices that don't handle jumbo fragments properly.

I'll try disabling TSO/GSO on a single host and repro.

-Jonas
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: alan.zhou@acme-corp.com, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 13:18:45 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures from our app -> Redwood private nodes (port 443)

Quick update: I grepped the iptables diff for Acme's per-customer chain. No explicit MSS clamp rules on our NAT path. We do have postrouting SNAT and conntrack. The host kernel doesn't show any iptables mss-clamp module loaded. dmesg on redd-az2-nf-17 includes a few 'ip_fragment: short packet' warnings around the timestamps in the pcap.

Actioned: I've disabled TSO/GSO on redd-az2-nf-17 and re-ran the same client workload against it. Early results: connection failures dropped to near zero in a 30k-conn test.

Next steps: coordinate with Acme to change their ASA MSS clamp (or disable on their egress) OR we can add a per-customer MSS clamping rule on our SNAT path as a workaround. Thoughts?

-Marissa
From: Alan Zhou <alan.zhou@acme-corp.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: netops@acme-corp.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 14:03:09 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures from our app -> Redwood private nodes (port 443)

Thanks for the fast triage team. We did a config review on our ASA and found an MSS clamping rule that's been in place for a long time (set to 1400) to protect an old MPLS link. We can remove it, but that might affect legacy paths. Netops suggests we disable it for sessions to Redwood's egress ASN only (they can match by destination subnet).

If you prefer, we can leave our rule and you add the MSS clamp on your SNAT path so the sessions are consistent end-to-end — either way works for us.

Alan
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: alan.zhou@acme-corp.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures from our app -> Redwood private nodes (port 443)

Thanks everyone — root cause and mitigation locked in: interaction between host offload (TSO/GSO) and a legacy MSS clamp on Acme's ASA caused mismatched segment sizes, which hit an intermediate device that couldn't reassemble/forward the larger frames. Disabling TSO/GSO on the affected hosts eliminated the symptom.

For the remediation plan we agreed on the call:
- Short-term (today): we'll push a per-customer iptables mangle POSTROUTING rule to set TCPMSS 1400 for traffic destined to Acme subnets (rolled via canary to two hosts then fleet).
- Mid-term (within 2 weeks): Acme removes or scopes their ASA MSS clamp for Redwood-local flows (Alan to schedule).
- Long-term: add e2e test to our private deployment checklist that includes MSS/TCP offload verification for new host images and enable a monitoring alert for increased SYN retransmits per-account. (Jonas + Marissa)

I've logged the follow-ups in JIRA NET-4021 and attached the captures and path traces to the ticket. Closing the active escalation; will watch metrics over the week.

Appreciate the quick coordination.

--
Rafael Mendes
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: acme_tcpdump-port443-20261128.pcap, path-trace-logs.txt
